stem:
During a scheduled review of a healthy 5-month-old boy, you note that his head circumference is 46 cm (>98th percentile) and his length and weight are on the 50th percentile. He has mild frontal bossing and widely split cranial sutures. The anterior fontanelle is flat. Arm and leg movements, tone, power and reflexes are normal. Reviewing prior growth parameters shows that his head circumference was at the 75th percentile at birth and the 90th percentile at 2 months.

Which of the following is the most appropriate initial investigation?

options.text: Lumbar puncture (LP) with manometry to measure pressure

explanation: A rapidly increasing head circumference in a 5-month-old with a still-open fontanelle and no focal neurological signs is appropriately assessed first with cranial ultrasound. This is a good initial, non-invasive test to look for hydrocephalus, extra-axial fluid, or other intracranial pathology before proceeding to more advanced imaging.
rationale: The key issue is progressive macrocephaly in an infant with an open fontanelle and normal examination. Cranial ultrasound is the most appropriate initial investigation.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Cranial ultrasound is the best initial investigation in an infant with macrocephaly and open fontanelle.
optionExplanations.B: Not first-line here. LP is not the initial investigation for macrocephaly and could be inappropriate if raised intracranial pressure is possible.
optionExplanations.C: Useful if ultrasound is abnormal or if further detail is needed, but not the initial test in this infant.
optionExplanations.D: Plain skull X-ray is not useful for assessing intracranial causes of macrocephaly.

Instructions

Question 4 - 6 relate to this quiz

Case 2

A 5-year old girl is brought in by her mother to see you because her teacher has been concerned that she has been having ‘day-dreams’ in choir practise and also during class. Her mother has also noted ‘day dreams’ which have been occurring mid-sentence associated with staring off in the distance. The ‘day dreams’ last a few seconds and then she is back to normal and continues on with her sentence. She doesn’t fall and doesn’t get sleepy after the events. She has no colour change. The girl is otherwise developmentally normal and got a good mid-year report from school. On examination her height and weight are on the 75

th

centile. She has a completely normal examination. You get the patient to blow up a balloon in your office and she has a staring spell that lasts 5seconds before she completely recovers.
